owner.name: Benjamin
owner.headline: I build useful software for complex, real-world problems.
owner.intro: I’m a Computer Science & Engineering student interested in the space between intelligent systems and thoughtful product engineering. I work across full-stack applications, applied machine learning, data workflows and edge devices — with a bias toward practical things that can be tested, shipped and improved.

projects.name: AWARESPAN
projects.summary: An AI-powered safety device designed to bring local threat detection and connected alerts to edge hardware.
projects.description: AWARESPAN explores a modular, on-premise safety system built around a Raspberry Pi node. The current work focuses on local visual threat detection, a separable processing pipeline and a foundation for reliable alerts without requiring the node to expose itself directly to mobile clients.

projects.name: Siddhi
projects.summary: A role-aware platform with dedicated views for students and guardians, designed around useful information and clear navigation.
projects.description: Siddhi is a full-stack application being developed with an emphasis on clear role-specific experiences, report views and a consistent application shell. The work includes frontend architecture, database-backed features and the details that make a product feel coherent across screens.

projects.name: AI-IDA
projects.summary: A detection pipeline for suspicious internship and job opportunities across messaging and email channels.
projects.description: AI-IDA investigates how structured message metadata and unstructured content can be combined to identify potentially fraudulent opportunities. The approach includes data collection and cleaning, duplicate and forwarded-message handling, text representations, classification and a semantic explanation layer.

projects.name: ClipZ
projects.summary: A lightweight desktop video editor designed to stay usable on low-spec PCs.
projects.description: ClipZ is a small-footprint video-editing concept with a simple Tkinter interface and a deliberate focus on minimal dependencies and straightforward distribution. The project avoids heavyweight AI features in favour of a practical desktop tool.
